title: KPI Dashboard Data Specs and Sample Sheet
content:
Purpose and scope:
This sheet is a compact data specification for the Customer Success KPI dashboard used in quarterly business reviews (QBRs) and renewal conversations. It defines canonical metric definitions (latency, uptime, cost/token, cache hit rate), recommended calculation windows and aggregation rules, and provides a sample table layout with example rows and suggested CS actions tied to thresholds.

Why this exists:
- Remove ambiguity between monitoring (SRE) and commercial metrics (CS) by standardizing formulas and aggregation windows.
- Make QBR sheets exportable from the metrics pipeline with predictable column semantics.
- Provide operationalizable action triggers so playbooks map to measurable signals.

Data sources (authoritative):
- Latency and cache: Prometheus histograms + request logs (ingest via metrics pipeline).
- Uptime: PagerDuty/heartbeat monitoring + scheduled maintenance calendar (source of truth: SRE roster calendar).
- Cost/token: Billing exports (model pricing) joined with token counts from usage-telemetry.
- Customer mapping: Identities from account-service (account_id) and product-route tags.

Measurement windows and cadence:
- Primary window: rolling 30d (default for QBR summaries).
- Short-term window: 7d (for recent regressions, early-warning).
- Baseline window: prior quarter 90d (for trend comparisons).
- Aggregation cadence: daily rollups; hourly for alerting dashboards.
- Outlier handling: drop top 0.1% tail per-day when computing daily p50/p90 to avoid skew from noisy spikes; retain tail for incident forensic logs.

Canonical metric definitions (single-line form + formula):
1) P50 Latency (ms) - per-request generation latency
   - Definition: Median end-to-end generation latency for successful text-generation requests (model returned 2xx).
   - Formula: P50 = median(request_generation_ms) on all successful requests in window after dropping top 0.1% daily tail.
   - Notes: exclude warmup/system-test traffic (tagged test=true).

2) P90 Latency (ms) - tail latency indicator
   - Definition: 90th percentile of generation latency for successful requests in window. 
   - Formula: P90 = 90th percentile(request_generation_ms) on window; report both raw P90 and trimmed P90 (excluding top 0.1% tail).

3) Uptime (%) - service availability for customer routes
   - Definition: Percentage of time the customer's configured API endpoints are available to serve requests (routing and model successful response), excluding approved scheduled maintenance.
   - Formula: Uptime = (total_time - downtime_excl_sched) / total_time * 100 over window.
   - Downtime sources: 5xx error spikes, routing failures, region-level outages.

4) Effective Cost / Token (USD/token) - blended per-token cost charged to customer (used for econ conversations)
   - Definition: Weighted average cost per token across request mix (model variant, quantization profile, batch size) for tokens generated + input tokens if applicable.
   - Formula: Cost/token = (sum over requests of model_unit_cost(request) * request_tokens) / (sum over requests of request_tokens). Model_unit_cost is derived from billing pricebook for the model variant and effective infra multiplier (dedicated vs hosted).
   - Notes: maintain separate columns for 'raw_billing_cost' and 'effective_cost_after_discounts' for reconciliation.

5) Cache Hit Rate (%) - prefix / KV cache efficiency
   - Definition: Fraction of requests where >50% of tokens were served from cache (prefix or KV) rather than fresh decoding.
   - Formula: CacheHitRate = (#requests with cached_token_count >= 0.5 * total_generated_tokens) / total_requests * 100.
   - Alternative metric: Token-level cache hit = cached_tokens / generated_tokens (useful for heavy-token workloads).

Column schema for the sheet (one flat row per customer per-window):
- customer_name
- account_id
- window_start (YYYY-MM-DD)
- window_end (YYYY-MM-DD)
- p50_latency_ms
- p90_latency_ms
- uptime_percent
- cache_hit_rate_percent (request-level definition)
- token_cache_hit_percent (optional, token-level)
- avg_cost_per_token_usd
- raw_billing_cost_usd
- effective_cost_after_discounts_usd
- total_requests
- total_generated_tokens
- sample_bias_flag (yes/no) - if traffic sampling applied
- notes (freeform)

Sample rows (three customers, 30d window ending 2026-02-01):
1) Acme Analytics | acct_00123 | 2025-12-03 | 2026-01-31 | p50=42 ms | p90=210 ms | uptime=99.98% | cache_hit_rate=62% | token_cache_hit=55% | avg_cost_per_token=$0.0009 | raw_billing=$4,200 | effective_cost_after_discounts=$3,780 | total_requests=1,120,432 | total_generated_tokens=4,720,980 | sample_bias_flag=no | notes=Stable; small p90 blip 2026-01-10 due to region failover.

2) BetaDocs Inc | acct_00456 | 2025-12-03 | 2026-01-31 | p50=135 ms | p90=1,240 ms | uptime=99.62% | cache_hit_rate=18% | token_cache_hit=12% | avg_cost_per_token=$0.0028 | raw_billing=$18,300 | effective_cost_after_discounts=$16,470 | total_requests=250,120 | total_generated_tokens=6,550,300 | sample_bias_flag=yes | notes=High p90 tail; retention task routes show multistep long generations.

3) Delta Retail | acct_00789 | 2025-12-03 | 2026-01-31 | p50=18 ms | p90=95 ms | uptime=99.995% | cache_hit_rate=82% | token_cache_hit=79% | avg_cost_per_token=$0.00045 | raw_billing=$980 | effective_cost_after_discounts=$980 | total_requests=420,210 | total_generated_tokens=1,820,100 | sample_bias_flag=no | notes=Good cache effectiveness from product-level prefixing; recommend exploring quantized model for further savings.

Threshold bands and suggested CS playbook actions (mapping to PS/SE/Sales triggers):
- Latency:
  - Green: p50 < 50ms AND p90 < 300ms -> no immediate action, include in standard QBR.
  - Yellow: p50 50-150ms OR p90 300-1000ms -> schedule performance review with Solutions Eng; investigate batching and prefix cache.
  - Red: p50 > 150ms OR p90 > 1000ms -> urgent SE + infra runbook; consider temporary routing to a smaller model variant or burst capacity.

- Uptime:
  - Green: >= 99.95% -> baseline SLA met.
  - Yellow: 99.5% - 99.95% -> open incident review; identify recurring sources.
  - Red: < 99.5% -> escalate to SRE and Customer Success Director; prepare remediation plan for renewal review.

- Effective cost per token:
  - Green: within 10% of expected baseline (customer tier) -> monitor.
  - Yellow: 10-30% above baseline -> propose cost-led optimizations (quantized models, longer cache live-times, batching).
  - Red: >30% above baseline -> commercial review with Sales for contract adjustments or migration to Dedicated pricing.

- Cache hit rate:
  - Green: request-level cache hit >= 60% (or token-level >= 50%) for prefix-heavy apps -> recommend retention/scaling playbook.
  - Yellow: 30-60% -> review prefix engineering and prompt templates; SE-run workshop.
  - Red: < 30% -> immediate SE audit and conversion playbook; consider design changes (structured caching, template normalization).

Notes on calculation hygiene and reconciliation:
- Keep raw event exports for the measurement window for independent audits; the sheet is an aggregation layer and must be reproducible from raw Prometheus + billing exports.
- Reconcile cost figures monthly — keep columns for raw_billing_cost and effective_cost_after_discounts to capture promotions or committed discounts.
- If traffic sampling is enabled for performance telemetry, append sample_bias_flag and include sampling_rate in the notes; do not compare sampled metrics directly to unsampled baselines.

Automation suggestions for the engineers team:
- Daily job (ETL): compute the per-customer daily rollups and write to a canonical BigQuery (or internal warehouse) table with the sheet columns.
- QBR export job: take 30d rolling window aggregates for each active account, attach previous-quarter baseline and delta columns, and produce CSV for CS.
- Alerts: wire p90 and uptime thresholds into CS incident routing (so CS receives a digest when a Yellow/Red condition first appears).

Open questions and follow-ups (for CS + Eng sync):
- Should we standardize the cache hit request-level definition at 50% of tokens, or make it configurable per vertical? (Action: CS to propose per-vertical thresholds by 2026-02-20).
- How do we handle multi-tenant Dedicated customers where infra costs are pooled? (Action: infra & finance to provide per-account cost allocation method).

Appendix: quick formula cheat-sheet (copyable into cells)
- p50_latency_ms: =PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5, generation_ms) after daily trimming
- p90_latency_ms: =PERCENTILE_CONT(0.9, generation_ms)
- uptime_percent: = (total_time - downtime_excl_sched)/total_time*100
- cache_hit_rate_percent (request level): =100 * COUNT_IF(cached_tokens >= 0.5 * generated_tokens) / COUNT(request_id)
- avg_cost_per_token_usd: = SUM(model_unit_cost * generated_tokens)/SUM(generated_tokens)
